get.description:
Simulate for N hours, returning hourly snapshots.

``hours`` outside 1-168 is rejected with 422 by request validation (it used
to reach the service and surface as a 500). The simulation is CPU-bound, so
it runs in a worker thread instead of blocking the event loop.

``utilisation``/``outside_temp`` are the run's means; compute_simulation
builds a diurnal curve around each rather than holding them flat for the
whole period.

``server_utilisation`` in each element is a fraction of capacity in [0, 1] (ADR 004).

T14: this GET writes NOTHING by default. ``persist=true`` (operator only) stores one SimulationRun plus one
SensorReading per simulated hour (<= 168 rows). Concurrency and time are bounded (api/rate_limit.py
``run_compute``): 429 when too many compute-heavy requests run, 504 on timeout.

get.description:
Stateless PREVIEW of one twin step for the given inputs. If mode='auto',
uses rule-based selection.

This is a what-the-twin-would-do-now calculation, not the live state (the
live state is what the WebSocket broadcasts). It runs on a throwaway twin
(``live=False``), so it does not advance the shared live twin, does not
touch its clock/thermal state/cumulative counters, and persists nothing.
``server_utilisation`` in the response is a fraction of capacity in [0, 1], never a percentage (ADR 004).

Because the twin is fresh on every call, cumulative fields such as
``water_consumed_L`` reflect a single step, not the live accumulator.

get.description:
Run an isolated 24 h digital-twin scenario at constant inputs and return its
aggregate PUE / WUE / water / energy / CO2. Nothing is persisted and the
shared live twin is not touched.

Parameter precedence: explicit query value > ``scenario_id`` preset > built-in default
(utilisation 0.65, outside_temp 22, water_stress 0, mode auto, chilled_water_temp 7). ``chilled_water_temp`` must lie in
the running physics' range (``SR.accepted_chilled_water_range``: 5-15 C under legacy-0, 5-25 C under physics 1). The response
echoes ``scenario_id`` (null for a raw what-if) and the resolved ``inputs``, and names the ``physics_version`` and the
``provenance`` (simulated origin, constant-input weather, registry and API versions) it came from. An unknown
``scenario_id`` is a 404, never silently ignored.

post.description:
Authenticate and return a short-lived access token plus a refresh
token. Rate limited: 10/minute per IP.

Revoke a refresh token so it can no longer be used to mint new
access tokens. Idempotent: revoking an already-revoked/unknown token
still returns 204, since the caller's goal (this token no longer
works) is already true.

Exchange a valid, unrevoked refresh token for a new access token and
a new refresh token (the old refresh token is revoked -- see the
module docstring's "Refresh tokens" section).

Create a new user with hashed password. Default role: viewer. Rate limited: 5/hour per IP.

Role "operator" requires header ``X-Admin-Key`` matching the
OPERATOR_REGISTRATION_KEY env var (403 otherwise, and always 403 if the
variable is unset -- operator self-registration is then disabled).

When public registration is disabled (ALLOW_PUBLIC_REGISTRATION, see
``public_registration_enabled``; the default in production) this returns
403 unless a valid ``X-Admin-Key`` is supplied -- that is how an
administrator provisions accounts without opening sign-up to everyone.

Single-use, opaque, short-lived (``WS_TICKET_TTL_SECONDS``, default 30). 503 if no ticket store is usable;
the frontend then falls back to the token flow.

get.description:
DEPRECATED alias (T18): use /livez (process alive) and /readyz (can serve traffic). Behaviour unchanged.

Unauthenticated liveness/readiness check for infrastructure (Docker
HEALTHCHECK, load balancers, uptime monitors) -- deliberately separate
from GET /api/health, which requires a JWT and exists for authenticated
clients confirming the API is reachable, not for infrastructure that
has no way to hold a token.

Returns HTTP 503 (not 200-with-a-status-field) when the DB is
unreachable, so a plain `curl -f` correctly detects failure -- a 200
response with a "degraded" string inside it would NOT fail curl -f,
and would make the Docker HEALTHCHECK below meaningless.

Process liveness (T18). Depends on NOTHING: no database, no auth, no Redis, no models. If this answers, the
event loop is running; whether the app can do useful work is /readyz's question.
